To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) The bandgap of ferroelectric complex-oxide BLT is reduced from 3.4 eV to 2.4 eV and 2.2 eV by Fe and Co doping.

1) the bandgap of BLT can be significantly reduced via Fe, Co doping; 2) this bandgap reduction results in enhanced light absorption in the visible region; 3) the photocurrent of the Fe, Co-doped BLT film is enhanced by more than 25 times compared with that of the undoped BLT film.
1) the bandgap can be tuned by doping transition metals into complex oxides and 2) this leads to a significant improvement of the photovoltaics performance of the material.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new class of ferroelectric materials with a reduced bandgap and enhanced photovoltaic effect.
the realization of a bandgap reduction in ferroelectric thin films by doping with Fe, Co.
the development of new functional materials for solar energy conversion, in particular for the use of ferroelectric materials in photovoltaics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bandgap reduction of the ferroelectrics by doping is an effective way to increase the visible light absorption and the photovoltaic performance.
the large bandgap reduction in ferroelectric oxides by transition metal doping leads to enhanced visible-light absorption and photocurrent generation.
the band gap of the ferroelectic complex oxides can be tuned by simple doping.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the band gap of a ferroelectric oxide can be reduced by more than 50% by doping with a transition metal element.
we have demonstrated that doping is an effective way to tune the bandgap in complex oxide materials and to improve their photovoltaic performance.
the bandgap reduction of BLFCT film by Fe doping and Co doping leads to an enhancement of the visible light absorption and a significant enhancement of the photocurrent density.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bandgap in wide-bandgap ferroelectric materials can be tuned by doping.
the bandgap of a complex oxide can be reduced by doping, leading to a large improvement of the photoelectric properties.
bandgap reduction in ferroelectric oxides by doping can significantly enhance the photovoltaic properties of the materials.
